I will still plant all 7 mu in cotton. I have done cotton for many years, so I will not change to something risky. At the start of the season I will first look at what I did last year, then adjust a little by cost and by how the field looked. With 7 mu and only 2 people at home, I need a way that is steady and not too labor-heavy. I have well irrigation, so I do not fear drought as much, and that lets me push fertilizer a bit to protect yield. I am middle-school educated, so I do count inputs and output. Cotton eats fertilizer for a long season, especially nitrogen and potash, but if I push nitrogen too hard the plants grow too wild, so I will keep nitrogen at a level that supports yield but does not make too much vegetative growth. I will use improved seed, because around Hebei many people have already shifted away from old seed, and if neighbors get better stand and cleaner bolls, I will follow that. For land prep, I will plough once before sowing, because cotton roots better in a loosened field than in hard ground. On fertilizer, I will set a base rate first, then topdress later if the stand is strong. On water, I will irrigate around key times: after establishment if dry, at budding, flowering, and boll setting. On pesticide, I will not save too much money there, because once aphids, red spider, or bollworm get ahead, yield drops fast. My goal is not the highest possible yield on paper. I will aim for a stable crop I can manage well on 7 mu with the labor and cash I have.
